creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The feature ships today and nobody found it. Three of the review's six assessors independently proposed it, two of them as a new feature - and the assessor that had the documenting page saved to disk the whole time still hand-rolled jq plus per-file checks. Its round-2 critic called that the opposite of motivated reasoning. This is a discoverability failure, not a capability gap.

Discoverability shapes the reports sketched: a rate-limited hint when an invoked script has outstanding check errors, an after-N-invocations variant, and a post-upgrade hint ("rad was upgraded across a breaking version; run `rad check --from-logs 90d`").

Four real gaps beyond discoverability:

- **Directory scan.** Nine of eleven broken scripts in one corpus have zero log entries. Three of seven agent-facing bin tools have never been logged and are structurally invisible to a log-keyed sweep.
- **Per-diagnostic detail.** The sweep prints counts, so "why is it broken" still means re-running per script.
- **`rad_version`-era reporting.** The log already records the interpreter version. Surfacing "broke since v0.7" is how the review dated `argus` to v0.9.0.
- **Near-miss shebang detection.** `sess` was invisible to every sweep because its shebang says `radd`. A real Rad script with 11 diagnostics, unselectable by anything keyed on the shebang, found only by reading a directory listing.

A `--fix` codemod is the natural follow-on and is deliberately not in this card. Two design inputs for when it comes: some rewrites must insert lines (`request` becomes `rad` plus `noprint`), and pre-v0.9 grammar deaths that surface as generic "Invalid syntax" aren't auto-fixable without an old-grammar parser.

---

### Orientation
- `rad check` is itself a Rad script: `core/embedded/check`, compiled into the binary. Its args block is lines 5-11 and the `--from-logs` branch is line 14.
- The heavy lifting is an **internal** builtin, `_rad_check_from_logs`, implemented at `core/funcs_internal_check_from_logs.go:52`. Internal `_rad_*` functions do **not** follow the docs-first flow - their signatures are hand-listed in `rts/signatures.go` (this one at `rts/signatures.go:71`, the sibling `_rad_run_check` at `:69`) and they deliberately have no `docs/funcs/` entry.
- Adding a new internal function means: const in `core/funcs.go` (the `INTERNAL_FUNC_*` block, e.g. `INTERNAL_FUNC_CHECK_FROM_LOGS` at `core/funcs.go:150`), a `BuiltInFunc` in `core/funcs_internal.go`, and a hand-written line in `rts/signatures.go`.

### Watch out for
- Any nudge printed at script exit runs on the hot path of every single `rad` invocation. `RegisterInvocationLogging` already guards on `RConfig.InvocationLogging.Enabled`; a nudge needs its own persisted rate-limit state and its own config switch, or it becomes the next thing people disable.
- Time and filesystem access must go through the seams: `RClock` is already used for the cutoff (`core/funcs_internal_check_from_logs.go:296`), not `time.Now()`. Keep new code consistent so `core/testing/` stays deterministic.
- Directory scanning is unbounded work in a way the log sweep is not. Decide on depth limits, ignore rules, and symlink handling before writing the walk.
- A `--fix` codemod is explicitly out of scope for this card - don't let it creep in.
title: Make rad check --from-logs findable, and add a directory scan
